title: Database & Data Architecture

seo.title: Database & Data Architecture | Julie Zimmerman
seo.description: Database and data architecture for migrations, synchronization, APIs, integrity, and privacy-preserving systems.

hero.headline: Designing data systems that preserve meaning while they move.
intro: I build data pipelines, schemas, synchronization systems, and migration strategies for environments where stale or malformed data has immediate operational consequences.

My background includes Oracle enterprise systems, MySQL and MariaDB applications, SQL Server and FileMaker integrations, RETS and RESO real-estate feeds, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets exceeding one million records.

philosophy.title: Engineering Philosophy
philosophy.anchor: Data architecture is the discipline of keeping meaning intact across systems, time, and scale.
philosophy.intro: A correct schema reflects the real business rules, not just the current screen.
principles: Imports and migrations need explicit validation and recovery paths.
Synchronization should make freshness, ownership, and failure visible.
Privacy can often be protected through architecture rather than policy alone.
philosophy.closing: Privacy can often be protected through architecture rather than policy alone.

problems.title: Problems I Solve
problems.intro: The most valuable work usually begins where a system has accumulated complexity, operational risk, or assumptions no one has revisited.
items: Legacy database analysis and migration planning

approach.title: How I Work
paragraphs: I trace data from source to consumer before changing it. That includes field semantics, timing, transformations, identifiers, permissions, and the behavior of downstream systems.
I design for partial failure: resumable imports, validation checkpoints, useful logs, and clear distinctions between source truth, derived data, and cached presentation.

evidence: Technical standards, migration planning, launch QA, and incident response

business_value.title: Why data integrity matters
paragraphs: A pipeline can run successfully while still delivering the wrong meaning. Reliable architecture tests more than transport: it verifies semantics, freshness, completeness, and downstream behavior.
That discipline reduces customer-facing errors, failed migrations, and the hidden cost of reconciling systems after trust has been lost.

closing_statement: Moving data is easy. Preserving its meaning is the engineering work.
